_comment: Lunda Grade 1 Learner's Book — per-book overrides.
Every entry here corrects this manuscript's own slips or sizes this manuscript's
own pictures. None of it is an engine fault, so none of it belongs in src/typeset/.
_comment_authors: The manuscript names the same person two ways: its own title page (line 5 of the
plain-text conversion) has the initials 'C.K. KABALAKANYA', while the ANSONEKI
bio page gives him in full as 'Charles Kazembe Kabalakanya, Managing Director/CEO
Wa Charle-Charle General Dealers Company Limited'. House style is one form per
person, the fullest one, so the cover and title-page byline carry the full name
rather than the initials the author happened to type on his own cover page.
_comment_localLabels: Local-language book: every label on the cover, title page and running header in Lunda, from lexicon/lunda.json
(level 'Shikola yamañu yanyanya mañu 1 - 6', book type 'Mukanda wa Kadizi') - the wording the 6 Oct typeset carried.
_comment_images: Four worksheet pictures the author drew PORTRAIT. The template caps a tall picture
by height so that one picture cannot swallow a whole page — a sound rule, and the
right one for a tall photograph. These four are not photographs: they are whole
worksheets, with their own word cards, writing rules and lettering inside them, and
each is the only thing on its page. At the template's standard cap they came out
63-86mm wide on a 142mm measure — a third to a half of the measure — with their
lettering too small for a Grade 1 reader, and two thirds of the page left blank
So each is given its own printed height instead. The heights below are chosen to
fill the page these pictures actually have while leaving the heading stack above
them room, and to keep the widest of them just inside the 142mm measure:
Printing them this size drops them below 300 DPI, so all four are upscaled — see
the upscale entries written by tools/upscale-images.js alongside this comment.
_comment_cover: COVER PICTURE. The manuscript opened with the same cartoon group photo the
Teacher’s Guide uses, which showed no learner with a disability — against the
house rule that every cover include one. This replacement, supplied for this book,
puts four learners at a reading table: a girl with albinism and a boy using a
wheelchair alongside two other learners, two girls and two boys.
The supplied file is a whole cover PAGE, not a photo: it carries an empty title
panel, an empty rainbow oval and a decorative border, all of which the template
draws itself. Left in, the hero card would have printed empty frames inside it. So
only the classroom scene is used, cropped to the hero card’s own 132x78mm
(1.692:1) so `fit: "cover"` has nothing left to trim: the crop already ends where
the card ends, which keeps every child, the wheelchair and its wheel in frame.
cropped    1033x610   the classroom scene alone, at the card’s aspect
upscaled   1600x945   Real-ESRGAN x4 then resampled down, 308 DPI at 132x78mm
lunda-g1-lb-cover-src.png is the crop before upscaling, kept because the upscale
cannot be reproduced from the supplied file alone if the card geometry ever changes.
_comment_manuscript: 2026-10-28: the manuscript now carries the author's edited version (a Word PDF of 26 Oct 2026 made from our
typeset book): end-of-chapter tests (KWESEKA KWAHACHIBALU) in Ch 1-7, Mudimu exercises in Ch 1-8, sound/syllable lessons
in Ch 6, 7, 9-12, the noun lessons renamed (mazhina ayuma / kala mazhina), listening lessons moved one topic earlier, and
story-based reading lessons in Ch 9-11. The author also renumbered the three "Zhakwila 1: Kusumbwisha" activities to 2,
so the editAll that used to do it here is gone.
2026-10-31: the author's second pass ("FINAL BOOK", a Word PDF of 27 Oct 2026) written into the manuscript the same way:
the Ch 11-14 noun lessons renamed IZHINA AWUMU NI AMAVULU (mazhina awumu / aamavulu), YISHIMUTWIZHI -> TUHEKA (Kaheka:),
MWALUMBULUKILA IZU -> MAZU, KWESEKA KWAHACHIBALU tests for Ch 8-14, more Mudimu exercises in Ch 10-14, Ch 5 retitled ÑENDELU,
two writing lessons retitled KUSONEKA NSONA, Kukopolola for Kukopa, and spellings (yiwunamoni, yinjikizhilu, chidikwikala, Iha).
_comment_hyphenate: A Grade 1 reader: no word is broken across two lines. Typst has no Lunda patterns, so its breaks were
_comment_indentLists: The tests and Mudimu exercises put i./ii. sub-items under a numbered question; without this they sat flush
with the numbers. indentLists nests them under their question, as the author's own version shows them.
_comment_pageBreakBefore: Four activity boxes that otherwise leave their last line or two (or their worksheet table) at the top

Ch 7 Talilenu nakusoneka Mazu ('2. Kulanda / 3. Maliketi'), Ch 11 Kutuña Yikunku Yamazu (its grid), Ch 12 Kuhimpa
Nikufumishaku ('3. Kudila / 4. Kutukana'). The first 'Kutuña Mazu Akuhosha' in the book is Ch 6's.
Also Ch 11 Kutaña Chati and Ch 12 Kwiluka Yikunku Yamazu Yidi Mwizu: their tables went to the next page without them.

The Ch 14 reading-lesson Mudimu (Kudihi kumwatela...) also starts a fresh page: its question 2 sat alone at the top of the next page.
